Dicyclomine Hydrochloride: One of the most widely used anticholinergic antispasmodics for IBS and infant colic (no longer recommended under 6 months). First approval/introduction: Synthesised c.1945 (William S. Merrell Company); marketed 1952; INN dicycloverine. Aluminium Hydroxide + Magnesium Hydroxide (Magaldrate-type antacid): Classic non-systemic antacid combination balancing aluminium-induced constipation with magnesium-induced laxation. First approval/introduction: Pharmacopoeial (IP/BP/USP). Simethicone (Activated Dimethicone): A physiologically inert antifoaming agent used for flatulence, bloating and before endoscopy. First approval/introduction: In use since the 1950s; INN added 1999.
Strengths not stated in product list (refer to pack label)
Antacid neutralises acid; simethicone relieves gas; dicyclomine relieves smooth-muscle spasm – comprehensive relief of dyspeptic and colicky symptoms.

Dicyclomine Hydrochloride Antimuscarinic action plus direct smooth-muscle relaxant effect, relieving GI and biliary colic and spasm. Receptor / target profile: Antimuscarinic (relatively M1-selective) plus direct smooth-muscle relaxant activity.

Aluminium Hydroxide + Magnesium Hydroxide (Magaldrate-type antacid) Neutralises gastric acid, raises intragastric pH and reduces pepsin activity; magnesium (laxative) and aluminium (constipating) effects balance each other. Receptor / target profile: Neutralises gastric HCl; aluminium hydroxide also binds bile acids and phosphate.

Simethicone (Activated Dimethicone) Lowers surface tension of gas bubbles in the GI tract so they coalesce and are expelled, relieving bloating and flatulence. Receptor / target profile: Non-systemic surfactant that lowers surface tension of gas bubbles so they coalesce and are expelled.
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax 1–1.5 h. Half-life ~1.8 h (initial). Excreted mainly in urine.

Dicyclomine Hydrochloride: Urinary retention, IOP in susceptible patients.
Aluminium Hydroxide + Magnesium Hydroxide (Magaldrate-type antacid): Mg and phosphate in renal impairment.

Dicyclomine Hydrochloride: Anticholinergic toxicity – dry hot skin, dilated pupils, tachycardia, delirium. Supportive care. Aluminium Hydroxide + Magnesium Hydroxide (Magaldrate-type antacid): Hypermagnesaemia in renal failure; supportive care. Simethicone (Activated Dimethicone): Not toxic.
Evidence derives from component data: antacids for dyspepsia, simethicone for bloating, dicyclomine for IBS spasm (Page & Dirnberger, 1981).
